data.body:
AC3 TRACKING (measured, not asserted) - the net-negative-lines criterion is currently FAILING and may be unachievable as written. Measured across the three merged consolidation children with 'git show --numstat' over non-test files: 6f18/55e308eaaf net +53, 4329/b46a901937 net +71, 111a/952ad4a0a6 net -1. COMBINED NET = +123 (416 added, 293 deleted).

The per-file breakdown shows consolidation IS doing its job and the metric is the problem. Every CALL SITE shrinks: compact_trigger -31, enrich_drain -31, push_state -25, close_precheck -44, claim -14, transition -15, doctor_locks -7, hlc -4. The entire positive term is the new owner module in each case: _store/paths.py +149, _commands/lifecycle_cascade.py +100, close_disposition.py +43. Extraction RELOCATES the duplicated body into one place and then has to document it - and the plan-review and code-review gates both demand that 'why' rationale, so stripping the docstrings to make the number go negative would be actively harmful and would trade a real quality signal for a proxy one.

Net line count only goes negative when a consolidation deletes enough copies to outweigh the single retained + documented owner. 6f18 removed five call-site derivations (-98) but its owner module is a full documented class, not the five one-liners it replaced.

NOT changing AC3 yet: n=3 of the consolidation children, and later children that collapse many copies (fcb7's failure classifier, d6e3's git retry policy) could still swing the aggregate negative. Re-measure with the full set before the epic closes. If it is still positive then, the honest fix is to correct the criterion to measure what consolidation actually means - one implementation per consolidated construct, which the per-child guard tests already enforce - with the line-count observation kept as advisory, rather than either forcing the number or quietly closing against a failed criterion.
